coverage.reason: Nothing on this page waits. docs/06-page-specs.md 7.0 states each state and why it does not exist: nothing is fetched, nothing can fail, and the page holds no data of its own.

coverage.evidence: Offline is identical to online: the page is static markup precached by the service worker, with no request that could fail, which docs/06-page-specs.md 7.0 names as the point - a page selling an offline-first app that could not be read offline would be its own refutation.

Each token added says what it is for rather than what it looks like: size-land-close for the closing line, size-land-section for a section heading, size-land-quote for the quotation, paper-ink and paper-line for the printed record that does not theme.

Every control and surface comes from ui/: LandingButton, Card, Rail, Icon, Mark, WordmarkArabic, IconButton and the new StackCard. The one hand-drawn control is the segmented switch in safe-to-spend-card.tsx:31, which is a drawing of a control inside a drawing of a screen, hidden from assistive technology with its reason beside it; the canvas draws it the same way, as .seg markup rather than a live control.

StackCard, the one shared component this branch adds, ships with its states: rest, hover and focus-visible all give the same 14px lift (tokens.css:330 and :368), and prefers-reduced-motion drops the movement and keeps the shadow (tokens.css:380).

Nothing means something by colour alone: the debt dot is aria-hidden with 'you owe' and 'owed to you' written beside it (landing-three-things.tsx:77-86), each comparison card names its side in words, and the ochre on the safe-to-spend card is accompanied by 'spending fast'.

Measured on the rendered page in the dark theme: soft on bg is 8.19:1 and soft on card2 is 6.81:1, both past AA for body text, with ink far above. The five new paper values were computed because they are new: #555 on #FFF is 7.46:1, #111 on #FFF is 19:1. The #CFCBC0 rule on white is 1.6:1 and is decoration inside a drawing of a document, not a control.

findings.title: The danger colour is on a page the spec says it is nowhere on
findings.evidence: rose is used three times - the 'The app you tried' label (landing-comparisons.tsx:140), the N75,000.00 figure in that card (:194) and the dot marking a debt you owe (landing-three-things.tsx:77). docs/design/11-landing-1440-light.png draws all three in red, and docs/standards/standards-addendum-mizaniya.md reserves the danger colour for money going wrong, with docs/06-page-specs.md:492 saying in as many words that it 'appears nowhere on this page'. The build followed the board, which CLAUDE.md section 7 makes authoritative on colour, and nobody recorded the disagreement until this review.
findings.fix: Put it to the designer and the spec owner in docs/open-items.md: either the boards' red becomes a non-danger tone on this page, or the addendum gains an exception for a surface where no figure is anyone's money and the spec's sentence goes. Change nothing until one of them answers.

findings.title: Four values on the page deliberately differ from the canvas
findings.evidence: The canvas is authoritative and these four do not match it: the four panels in 'The rest of it' scale their replicas at 0.64 where LandLight.dc.html sets zoom .68 (at .68 a 340px card is 231px inside a panel with 224px between its paddings, so the margin the board shows on either side disappears); band headings on a phone are 25px where LandPhoneLight sets 26px for a band and 25px for the hero; the comparison band's closing line is 13.5px where the phone canvas sets 12.5px; and the 'Safe to spend' sub-line is 17/29 where the phone canvas sets 15/24. All four are written down in docs/open-items.md section V for the designer.
findings.fix: The designer answers section V. Each is a one-line change once they do; none should be changed before.

findings.title: The landing page's scale and the paper colours live in the code and not in the published tokens
findings.evidence: tokens.css now declares thirteen landing type steps, seven of them added by this branch, plus five paper colours for the printed record, and docs/design/tokens.md publishes none of them. The document calls itself the token contract, so a reader who follows it sees a scale the page does not use. docs/open-items.md section T.4 raised this for the type, and section V.2 raises it for the paper colours; both are unanswered.
findings.fix: The designer decides, in section T.4 and V.2: publish them in tokens.md, which makes the document true again, or record that the landing scale is board-local and say so in tokens.md so the contract stops claiming to cover everything.

findings.title: The page's type does not follow the browser's text-size setting
findings.evidence: Every type step is a px value and index.css:13 sets the body to 15px, so a reader who has raised their browser's default text size sees no change; only zoom scales the page, which is what WCAG 1.4.4 asks for but not what the rule says. tokens.md section 5 makes the scale a 2px grid keyed to the pixel, so this is the design system's decision and the page follows it faithfully.
findings.fix: A question for the designer rather than a change to this page: whether the published scale should be expressed in rem against a 16px root, which keeps every drawn number and makes the whole app follow the setting.

summary: Pass, 4 medium open. The page was compared band by band with the 1440 and 390 boards in both themes, rendered through a headless browser: order, copy, measures and motion match. Open: the danger colour, which the boards draw and the spec says is nowhere here; four values deliberately off the canvas, recorded in open-items section V; the landing scale and paper colours living in code rather than tokens.md; and px type, which ignores the browser's text-size setting.
